questions.q: What is the underlying expression behind the design-surface shorthand [Sales]?
options: [Sales] has no underlying expression — it's just literal text
questions.explain: Dragging a field to the design surface creates the simple expression =Fields!Sales.Value, shown as the shorthand [Sales].

questions.q: How do you reference a report parameter named Store in an expression?
questions.explain: Parameters are referenced through the Parameters collection: =Parameters!Store.Value, shown as [@Store] on the design surface.

questions.q: What does the & operator do in an SSRS expression?
options: Comments out the rest of the expression
questions.explain: & is the string-concatenation operator — for example, Fields!FirstName.Value & " " & Fields!LastName.Value joins a first and last name with a space.

options: True if LineTotal is greater than 100, otherwise False
The numeric value of LineTotal minus 100
An error, because IIF requires three field references
questions.explain: IIF evaluates the condition first, then returns the second argument if true or the third if false — here, True when LineTotal exceeds 100, otherwise False.

questions.q: When would you reach for Switch instead of IIF?
options: When you have three or more conditions to test, rather than a single true/false test
Switch and IIF are identical and interchangeable in every case
Only when working with date values
Switch is deprecated and should never be used
questions.explain: Switch returns the value tied to the first of several conditions that evaluates to true, which is cleaner than nesting multiple IIFs when there are three or more outcomes.
